result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by narrow, obstructed sidewalks and a lack of formal crossing infrastructure. High levels of on-street parking on both sides further constrain the space and create potential visibility issues for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Waste bins and utility poles narrow the already tight walking space on the left sidewalk.

hazards.name: Lack of Crossing Infrastructure
hazards.description: No marked crosswalks or curb ramps are visible for pedestrians needing to cross the street.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Continuous on-street parking blocks sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and moving vehicles.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening
interventions.description: Increase the width of the sidewalks to provide a clear, unobstructed path for pedestrians, meeting ADA standards.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at potential crossing points to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Paint high-visibility crosswalks to designate safe crossing locations for pedestrians.

result.summary: The image shows a mid-block urban street with a paved sidewalk that is significantly narrowed by a large mature tree. Parallel on-street parking is present, which provides a physical buffer from moving traffic but also creates visual obstructions for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A large tree trunk occupies a significant portion of the sidewalk, creating a narrow pinch point that may hinder accessibility for wheelchairs or strollers.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles and the large tree trunk can obscure pedestrians from the view of drivers, especially if they attempt to cross mid-block.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line in the foreground and midground.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening
interventions.description: Expand the sidewalk width or create a curb extension around the tree to maintain a consistent and accessible clear path of travel.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking spaces immediately adjacent to the tree or near potential crossing points to improve sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a well-marked continental crosswalk and continuous sidewalks within a commercial district. While stop signs provide traffic control, the lack of physical traffic calming and the presence of parked cars near the crossing create potential visibility hazards.

hazards.name: Restricted sightlines from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Vehicles parked immediately adjacent to the crosswalk obscure the view between pedestrians entering the roadway and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground left and right, adjacent to the crosswalk markings.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian-specific signals
hazards.description: The intersection relies on stop signs without dedicated pedestrian signals to indicate when it is safe to cross.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the intersection to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines between motorists and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install lower-height lighting fixtures specifically oriented toward the sidewalk and crosswalk to improve nighttime safety.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with a paved sidewalk and a narrow planting buffer. Parallel parked cars line the curb, which creates a visual barrier between the walkway and the roadway.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: The line of parked cars obscures the view of pedestrians for drivers and vice versa, increasing risk at potential crossing points.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and middle ground along the curb line.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the nearest intersection to improve sightlines and reduce crossing distance.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add street lighting specifically oriented toward the sidewalk to improve visibility and security at night.
